summary: Verified the two deployment-blocker fixes for HexTribes. (1) Backend: /api/health returns HTTP 200 with body {"status":"ok"} via the public EXPO preview URL. Also confirmed /api/ root and top-level /health route (top-level path is served by the frontend through ingress, which is expected; the backend /health handler is meant for k8s probing :8001 directly and is not exposed by ingress). (2) Frontend smoke: Main menu renders with icons; menu-new-game -> Single Player -> start-game navigates into the game screen (testID game-screen); isometric map + HUD icons render; tapping action-end-turn twice advances the turn counter T1 -> T2 -> T3 with no blank/white/red/crash screen and zero page/console errors captured. types.ts compile fix is effective (bundle serves and app renders).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py uses datetime.utcnow() (deprecated in Python 3.12+). Prefer datetime.now(timezone.utc). Non-blocking for current task.

Top-level /health handler in server.py is unreachable via public ingress (non-/api paths route to frontend). This is fine for internal k8s probes on :8001, but if the intent was external liveness, prefer /api/health only.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend .env exposes EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (used by Expo web) rather than EXPO_BACKEND_URL. Use that for external testing. To bypass the first-run tutorial that overlays action-end-turn, set localStorage.hextribes_tutorial_seen_v1='true' before navigating to the game, or click the 'Skip' text on the tutorial overlay. AI turns can take up to ~15 seconds to resolve; poll the T# HUD label instead of using a fixed wait.
